turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Come on in and have a seat. I'll grab vitals while he's finishing up a note.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Thanks. I actually got here early. The parking garage was empty, which, um, never happens.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Enjoy it while it lasts. Date of birth, so I pull the right chart?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): March 12th, 1974. So fifty-one.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): Perfect. Relax this arm. Blood pressure is one thirty-eight over eighty-two, and your pulse is 56.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Fifty-six? Is that too slow? I don't know. Sorry, you're the nurse, not the doctor.
[SEG0007] person_1 (NURSE): It's on the slow side, not something I'd call urgent. Temperature's ninety-seven point four. Oxygen is 98 percent.
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, I believe the low temp. I've been freezing.
[SEG0009] person_1 (NURSE): Step on the scale for me. A hundred and eighty-one pounds. Last weight we have is a hundred and sixty-four, and that was a couple of years ago.
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): I thought I'd gained like ten pounds... no, if I was 164, that's more like seventeen. Huh. I don't know.
[SEG0011] person_1 (NURSE): You taking any medicines every day?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Vitamin D. I almost said a thousand units, but the bottle's two thousand, once a day. Ibuprofen sometimes if my knees ache, not every day.
[SEG0013] person_1 (NURSE): I'll put that in. He should be right in. I've got to open the next room.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hey, sorry about the wait. This thing logged me out mid-sentence. One second... okay, I think it's back. What brings you in?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm just exhausted. Bone tired. I kept telling myself it's the job.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Say that again? Screen flickered, I lost the first half.

[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Tired. I'm wiped out when I get home, even on quiet days. It's been three months... no, that's wrong. It was already going on before the holidays, so more like eight months.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Eight months. You said eight? I want to type it right this time.
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Eight. I don't know, doctor, maybe it's been creeping longer, but eight months is the honest answer.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): And work is what, exactly?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm a bookkeeper. Tax season about kills me every year, but this didn't ease up after April, so I can't pin the whole thing on April.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hold on, there's a refill alert and it's not even your chart. Stupid popup. Alright. What else is going on?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): I've been cold. Sweaters in the house. My husband swears the thermostat is fine and that it's me.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): Cold all the time, or off and on?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really. I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): Nurse has you at 181 today. You'd noticed the weight?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, nothing fits. I've been eating junk at my desk, and I'm fifty-one, so I blamed that.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): What about your bowels? Constipation, diarrhea, any change?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Constipation, yeah. I'm going maybe every three days and I have to strain. When it started, I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any blood in the stool?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I haven't seen any.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Fevers?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): How's your mood through all this?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Fine. I'm not depressed. It's not a mood thing, it's work and getting older.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hair thinning at all, or breaking more?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really. Hard to tell.
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sorry, say that once more? A page popped up and the note scrolled on me.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Hair. I said sometimes, not really. I don't know.
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'll leave it blank then. Anybody in the family with thyroid disease? I'm asking because of the fatigue.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): My mom. She had thyroid disease and took some pill for years. I couldn't tell you the name. She died in 2018, not from the thyroid, from a stroke, I think.
[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): Underactive, overactive, surgery?
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. No surgery, I don't think. Just the pill. I was a kid when it started, pretty much.
[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): Did anyone ever check your thyroid?
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): Once, yeah. They said the number was 7.2... no, wait, that's not it, they said borderline, something like 4-ish. I don't actually remember the number.
[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): And when was that test? I need you to repeat it, I clicked the wrong year box.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): 2019, or 2016, I really don't know which, so don't write a year down. They just called it borderline.
[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): Are you on any thyroid medicine now? Say it again, I was fighting the mouse.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): No thyroid medicine. Just the vitamin D, two thousand units a day, and ibuprofen here and there for the knees.
[SEG0050] person_3 (DOCTOR): The knees, is that a real problem or once in a while?
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): Not really often. Mostly after the stairs at the office. I don't know if it matters.
[SEG0052] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me feel your neck. Chin up a little.
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay, chin's up. Sorry, I talk when I'm nervous.
[SEG0054] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thyroid feels normal, I don't feel a goiter. Skin on your arms is a little dry, though.
[SEG0055] person_2 (PATIENT): Lotion's basically useless. Um, I need to walk something back.
[SEG0056] person_3 (DOCTOR): Go ahead. The order set is spinning, but I'm listening.

[SEG0057] person_2 (PATIENT): My mood. I told you I was fine and I'm not — I've been really down, I cry in the car after work sometimes, and I don't enjoy TV or seeing friends anymore. I don't know, doctor. I still think it's the job and my age, but it's there.
[SEG0058] person_3 (DOCTOR): I appreciate you correcting that. Any thoughts of hurting yourself?
[SEG0059] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing like that. I just feel flat.
[SEG0060] person_3 (DOCTOR): Okay. Putting it together, the fatigue, the weight, the constipation, your mom's thyroid, I'm thinking possible hypothyroidism. I can't say that for certain today.
[SEG0061] person_2 (PATIENT): So you're saying it's not just work?
[SEG0062] person_3 (DOCTOR): Work and age could still be in the mix. The low mood might be its own thing, too. That's on the differential, not a label I'm sticking on you.
[SEG0063] person_2 (PATIENT): Alright. I don't know, doctor. I just want to stop dragging through the day.
[SEG0064] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'll send labs. A TSH, a free T4, a CBC, and a basic metabolic panel.
[SEG0065] person_2 (PATIENT): Can that happen today? I've got a client call at two and I can't sit here all afternoon.
[SEG0066] person_3 (DOCTOR): The lab's down the hall, so it shouldn't eat your whole afternoon. We'll draw it today before you go. That's the plan, not a maybe.
[SEG0067] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. Are you starting me on a pill?
[SEG0068] person_3 (DOCTOR): No medicine from me until the results are back. Meanwhile, more water and some fiber for the constipation, and don't write the tiredness off as just getting older.
[SEG0069] person_2 (PATIENT): Fiber, got it. My sister is obsessed with those gummy fibers. They taste like candy, which seems like cheating. Anyway.
[SEG0070] person_3 (DOCTOR): Come back in about three weeks and we'll go through the labs together. If you feel worse before then, call the office.
[SEG0071] person_1 (NURSE): I can walk you to the lab whenever you're set. Printer jammed on the instructions, so give me a second to reprint.

spec.situation: Middle-aged person tired and cold for months, weight up, constipated, low mood; pins it on work and age; mother had thyroid disease; one old thyroid test result recalled wrongly ('borderline, they said'). Blood test planned.
features: doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).
ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.
self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.

denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Bookkeeper and tax season noted; 'long hours' not stated.
bad.text: occupation (description=Bookkeeper, status=current, details=Long hours, especially during tax season, reported_by=patient)

bad.reason: Prior thyroid test supported, but it was not requested by patient.
